text.content:
None of the Knot is about killing anything. All of it is about people arriving, and about Clipper being the reason they did.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Clipper)

Your Charges

The Trail Charges pool grows on its own at 6th, 10th and 15th level. You never have to update the sheet — the number just changes.

StateYour levelTrail ChargesBack at dawn
Dormantlevels 3–53all of them
Awakenedlevels 6–95all of them
Exaltedlevels 10–1471d6 + 1
Legendarylevel 15+91d8 + 1

At Dormant and Awakened every spent charge comes back. From 10th level it stops refilling completely: the pool is bigger, and a heavy day stays expensive into the next one.

Legacy Save DC

Where a feature makes something roll a saving throw, the DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier. It comes off your sheet, so it rises as you do.

What Unlocks When

Features arrive on their own. Below its level a feature is not on the item at all, so anything you can see on the sheet is something you can use. Where a later state improves an earlier feature, the old version disappears and the new one takes its place.

Dormant — levels 3–5 (Uncommon): Never Lost; Rope Remembers; Get Them Through.

Awakened — levels 6–9 (Rare): Follow Me; Find the Missing; Sure Footing.

Exalted — levels 10–14 (Very Rare): Waymarks; Walk My Road; I'm Coming Back.

Legendary — level 15+ (Legendary): There Is Always a Road; Nobody Gets Lost; Bring Them Home.

The Part That Is Not Automatic

Sure Footing ships switched off on the item. When the item awakens, ask your DM to enable it in the Effects tab — a passive like this cannot read your level the way the charge pool can.

Advancing

Reaching the level makes the next state possible. What actually wakes the item is the moment named at the top of each state below — a choice, not an achievement, and never something you can win in a fight. You do not need to chase it. When it happens, you will know, and so will the item.

Uncommon · levels 3–5 · 3 Trail Charges, all of them restored at dawn

Where it starts. This is the item as you first receive it. Everything below is yours from the moment you attune.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Never Lost

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

Clipper always knows north, and the direction and approximate distance to the place where he most recently completed a long rest, provided it is on the same plane. He has advantage on Survival checks to navigate and to follow tracks.

Rope Remembers

1 minute — no cost — 24 hours

Clipper can touch the Knot to a location for 1 minute. For 24 hours he knows its direction and approximate distance while on the same plane. Only one location can be remembered at a time.

Get Them Through

Bonus action — 1 charge

As a bonus action, Clipper can expend 1 charge and choose himself or one creature within 30 feet. Until the end of its next turn, difficult terrain costs it no additional movement, standing costs only 5 feet, and it does not provoke opportunity attacks from one creature Clipper chooses.

Rare · levels 6–9 · 5 Trail Charges, all of them restored at dawn

What wakes it. Clipper willingly gives up progress toward an important objective to return for someone or something that would otherwise be left behind.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Follow Me

No action — 1 charge

When Clipper takes the Dash action, he can expend 1 charge. Up to a number of willing creatures equal to his proficiency bonus, within 30 feet, can use their reactions to move up to half their speeds toward Clipper without provoking opportunity attacks.

Find the Missing

1 minute — 2 charges — 1 hour, concentration

Clipper can hold an object belonging to a creature, concentrate for 1 minute and expend 2 charges. For 1 hour he knows the general direction of that creature while it is within 5 miles on the same plane. If it is dead, he senses its remains instead. This does not reveal distance or obstacles.

Sure Footing

Passive. Always on once the item awakens — but it ships switched off, because a passive like this cannot read your level the way the charge pool does. Ask your DM to enable it in the item's Effects tab.

Clipper gains a climbing speed equal to his walking speed. This one passive is shipped as a switched-off effect on the item — enable Sure Footing in the item's Effects tab when the Knot awakens.

Very Rare · levels 10–14 · 7 Trail Charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Clipper successfully guides others through a journey from which he personally has compelling reason not to return.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Waymarks

10 minutes — no cost

Clipper can establish a number of permanent Waymarks equal to his proficiency bonus. Establishing one requires 10 minutes at the location. He always knows the direction and approximate distance to every Waymark while on the same plane. Creating one beyond his maximum erases one of his choice.

Walk My Road

Action — 3 charges — 1 hour

As an action, Clipper can expend 3 charges and choose up to his proficiency bonus in willing creatures within 30 feet. For 1 hour their walking speeds increase by 10 feet, nonmagical difficult terrain costs them no extra movement, they have advantage on checks and saves against environmental hazards caused by travel, and they cannot become lost except through powerful magical interference.

I'm Coming Back

No action — no cost

When a creature affected by Find the Missing is reduced to 0 hit points, Clipper immediately knows. For the remaining duration his speed increases by 10 feet whenever he moves directly toward that creature, and opportunity attacks against him have disadvantage.

Legendary · level 15+ · 9 Trail Charges, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Clipper must choose between completing an extraordinary journey and returning for someone who needs him — and chooses to return, knowing the opportunity may never come again.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

There Is Always a Road

1 minute — 5 charges · 1× per long rest — 10 minutes

Once per long rest, Clipper can spend 1 minute holding the Knot and expend 5 charges. Choose one of his Waymarks on the same plane within 100 miles. A shimmering trail appears; Clipper and up to eight willing creatures who follow it travel through an impossible shortcut and emerge at the Waymark after 10 minutes. This is not teleportation for mechanical purposes — the travellers physically traverse a supernatural road, and cannot interact with the outside world during the journey.

Nobody Gets Lost

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

All willing creatures within 30 feet of Clipper cannot become magically lost, know the direction to Clipper, and have advantage on saving throws against magical effects that would teleport or banish them against their will.

Bring Them Home

Action — 1× per long rest — 8 hours

Once per long rest, Clipper can designate up to six willing creatures he can see. For 8 hours he always knows their direction and approximate distance while they remain on the same plane. If one becomes unconscious, dies, changes planes or is forcibly teleported, Clipper knows immediately.

None of the Knot is about killing anything. All of it is about people arriving, and about Clipper being the reason they did.

At the Table

  • Never Lost costs nothing and never switches off. In any wilderness, underground or unfamiliar scene, say out loud that he knows north and the way back to camp. It changes what the party is willing to risk.
  • Get Them Through is the workhorse. One bonus action and one charge frees an ally from difficult terrain, halves the cost of standing up, and lets them leave a melee safely.
  • Find the Missing needs something of theirs. Collect a keepsake from each party member now, while nobody is missing.
  • Waymarks are permanent and scarce. There are only proficiency-bonus many. Spend them on places worth returning to, not on wherever he happens to be standing.
  • There Is Always a Road is not teleportation, so wards against teleporting do not stop it — but it takes ten real minutes and nobody can touch the world on the way.

Questions That Come Up

Does Follow Me move Clipper?
No. He takes the Dash action himself; the others spend their reactions moving toward him.

Can Sure Footing be used before 6th level?
No. It ships switched off on the item, and the DM enables it when the Knot awakens.

Does Find the Missing reach across planes?
No. Same plane, five miles, direction only — no distance and no obstacles.

Can There Is Always a Road reach a Waymark he did not walk to?
Any Waymark on the same plane within 100 miles, however it was made.

What happens if he makes one Waymark too many?
One of his existing Waymarks is erased, and he chooses which.

If Something Here Disagrees With the Item

The item on your sheet is the rules. This journal is generated from the same source, so the two should never differ — but if they do, the item wins and your DM should know.
